questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: A combination of the interesting subjects offered, meeting people from different cultures and having the possibility to explore a new country.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A bigger city with loads to explore and with values I liked.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I had all the information I needed. The only thing was that the campus was so big, so it was difficult to find the class rooms in the start.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Information from the booths around campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: None

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was much more difficult to find somewhere to live, than I would have thought. When the semester starts there are so many other students looking for housing, so the competition is really big. I would start looking for a place to stay as fast as possible.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very difficult to find somewhere to stay, but it is often cheaper if you are lucky to find a share-house. If you want to be sure to find something quick maybe try one of the many UniLodges. There are many international students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found it difficult to apply for subjects. The online system was hard to understand, and there was not much help to get, especially not before arriving to Melbourne.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First I had to find the subjects I wanted in the university's handbook. After receiving the CoE and making an account on the uni site, I could apply for the subjects. I had to wait for a long time before I knew if the subjects were approved. One subject ended up not being approved and I had to find another subjects, email professors and apply again in the first week of the semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I tried emailing the person responsible for exchange, but I didn't help much. I was happy I knew someone else from my home institution going to Melbourne too, so we could help each other.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was more difficult than I would have hope for. I got 3/4 of the subjects I really wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It seems very stressful to register for subjects when you are still at home, but I learnt that even though the systems might not work for you, you will always find a solution when you get to the host university.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had some very interesting courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had both level 1, 2 and 3 courses. There was a clear difference in difficulty level between the three course types.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I have been used to block structure, so I had to adjust to having more subjects for at longer period of time. Also, most of the subjects have obligatory assignments and tests throughout the semester. The professors of the courses can choose the style of teaching. Some of the courses remind me of UCPH with a combination of lectures and practicals, and other courses only have lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Cell Signalling and Neurochemistry, Stem Cells in Development & Regeneration, Food Nutrition and Health and Mind, Brain and Behaviour 2.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all my courses (Cell Signalling and Neurochemistry, Stem Cells in Development & Regeneration, Food Nutrition and Health and Mind, Brain and Behaviour 2). The professors are very passionate. Cell Signalling and Neurochemistry and Stem Cells in Development & Regeneration are quite difficult though.

questions.answer: Food is very expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Much more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They uni has clubs for most sports. They also have language and movies clubs for example.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The surf club is very popular and an easy way to meet international students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Experience the different suburbs in Melbourne. In a 2-3 hour (by car) radius from the city there are so many amazing nature spots.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Yes. I think the culture is very western, they are used to people from many cultures and everyone is so welcoming.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to find one of the very popular share-houses.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It is hard to get around by bike:)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That people are so kind and welcoming.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Make sure you attend some of the events at the start of the semester, as this is the easiest way to find friends.
- Apply for grants or bring your savings, because it is much more expensive than you would think. 
- This city is awesome!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use some of the very good libraries, apply for the free food program, try to join weekend tours out of the city and enjoy.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: At the end having found some good friends, made it well through the semester and learning so much personally along the way.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The start was the most difficult - arriving to a new city, not knowing anyone and having to adjust to a new way of studying.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
